    void verify_stock_mode()
    {
        check(installed_shell() == nullptr, "stock_mode_installs_no_shell");
        check(m_notebook->GetBtnsListCtrl()->IsShown(), "stock_mode_keeps_tab_strip");
        check(m_plater->is_sidebar_available(), "stock_mode_keeps_sidebar_available");
        load_multi_plate_fixture();
        check(m_plater->canvas3D()->get_volumes_count() >= 2, "stock_mode_canvas_renders_fixture");
        // Exiting with loaded volumes trips an inherited teardown crash in
        // ~GLCanvas3D (Selection::clear() re-enters the destroyed Plater);
        // see the Phase 1 handback. End on an empty project like the shell
        // scenario does.
        check(m_plater->new_project(true, true) != wxID_CANCEL, "stock_mode_teardown_project");
    }

    void verify_shell_installed()
    {
        ShellController* shell = installed_shell();
        check(shell != nullptr && shell->is_installed(), "shell_installed");
        if (shell == nullptr)
            throw std::runtime_error("shell is not installed");
        // Startup lands on Home, which shows no header and collapses the Agent
        // pane on the person's behalf. verify_agent_pane_follows_page checks
        // both return on Prepare, and checks the header's layout there.
        check(m_notebook->GetSelection() == MainFrame::tpHome, "shell_starts_on_home");
        check(shell->status_row() != nullptr && !shell->status_row()->IsShown(), "status_row_hidden_on_home");
        check(shell->status_row()->project_summary().Contains(wxString::FromUTF8("Prints \xC2\xB7 0")),
              "overflow_summary_shows_empty_print_count");
        verify_type_roles_render_at_token_size();
        check(shell->agent_pane() != nullptr && shell->is_agent_pane_collapsed() && !shell->agent_pane()->IsShown(),
              "agent_pane_collapsed_on_home");
        check(shell->agent_pane()->web_view().host().mcp() != nullptr, "shell_starts_mcp_automatically");
        check(!m_notebook->GetBtnsListCtrl()->IsShown(), "tab_strip_hidden");
        check(!m_plater->is_sidebar_available(), "sidebar_marked_unavailable");
        // The shell hides the entire legacy canvas-overlay layer on Prepare.
        check(m_plater->get_view3D_canvas3D()->legacy_overlays_hidden(), "prepare_legacy_overlays_hidden");

        // Later Orca paths call enable_sidebar(true); the persistent policy
        // must keep the sidebar down until the shell releases it.
        m_plater->enable_sidebar(true);
        check(!wxGetApp().sidebar().IsShown(), "sidebar_stays_hidden_after_reenable_attempt");

        // A second installation attempt must fail without disturbing layout.
        ShellController second;
        bool second_install_failed = false;
        try {
            second.install(*m_frame, *m_notebook, *frame_main_sizer());
        } catch (const std::exception&) {
            second_install_failed = true;
        }
        check(second_install_failed, "second_install_rejected");
        check(installed_shell()->is_installed() && installed_shell()->status_row()->GetContainingSizer() != nullptr,
              "shell_survives_rejected_install");
    }

    void verify_stock_mode()
    {
        check(installed_shell() == nullptr, "stock_mode_installs_no_shell");
        check(m_notebook->GetBtnsListCtrl()->IsShown(), "stock_mode_keeps_tab_strip");
        check(m_plater->is_sidebar_available(), "stock_mode_keeps_sidebar_available");
        load_multi_plate_fixture();
        check(m_plater->canvas3D()->get_volumes_count() >= 2, "stock_mode_canvas_renders_fixture");
        // Exiting with loaded volumes trips an inherited teardown crash in
        // ~GLCanvas3D (Selection::clear() re-enters the destroyed Plater);
        // see the Phase 1 handback. End on an empty project like the shell
        // scenario does.
        check(m_plater->new_project(true, true) != wxID_CANCEL, "stock_mode_teardown_project");
    }

    void verify_shell_installed()
    {
        ShellController* shell = installed_shell();
        check(shell != nullptr && shell->is_installed(), "shell_installed");
        if (shell == nullptr)
            throw std::runtime_error("shell is not installed");
        // Startup lands on Home, which shows no header and collapses the Agent
        // pane on the person's behalf. verify_agent_pane_follows_page checks
        // both return on Prepare, and checks the header's layout there.
        check(m_notebook->GetSelection() == MainFrame::tpHome, "shell_starts_on_home");
        check(shell->status_row() != nullptr && !shell->status_row()->IsShown(), "status_row_hidden_on_home");
        check(shell->status_row()->project_summary().Contains(wxString::FromUTF8("Prints \xC2\xB7 0")),
              "overflow_summary_shows_empty_print_count");
        verify_type_roles_render_at_token_size();
        check(shell->agent_pane() != nullptr && shell->is_agent_pane_collapsed() && !shell->agent_pane()->IsShown(),
              "agent_pane_collapsed_on_home");
        check(shell->agent_pane()->web_view().host().mcp() != nullptr, "shell_starts_mcp_automatically");
        check(!m_notebook->GetBtnsListCtrl()->IsShown(), "tab_strip_hidden");
        check(!m_plater->is_sidebar_available(), "sidebar_marked_unavailable");
        // The shell hides the entire legacy canvas-overlay layer on Prepare.
        check(m_plater->get_view3D_canvas3D()->legacy_overlays_hidden(), "prepare_legacy_overlays_hidden");

        // Later Orca paths call enable_sidebar(true); the persistent policy
        // must keep the sidebar down until the shell releases it.
        m_plater->enable_sidebar(true);
        check(!wxGetApp().sidebar().IsShown(), "sidebar_stays_hidden_after_reenable_attempt");

        // A second installation attempt must fail without disturbing layout.
        ShellController second;
        bool second_install_failed = false;
        try {
            second.install(*m_frame, *m_notebook, *frame_main_sizer());
        } catch (const std::exception&) {
            second_install_failed = true;
        }
        check(second_install_failed, "second_install_rejected");
        check(installed_shell()->is_installed() && installed_shell()->status_row()->GetContainingSizer() != nullptr,
              "shell_survives_rejected_install");
    }

// Contract tests for the viewport tool strip's layout: a row in the canvas's
// upper-left corner, and where each button sits in it, independent of the
// selection and the camera.

#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>

#include "slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Canvas/ViewportToolStripLayout.hpp"

#include <cmath>

using namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin;

namespace {

// The token file's values: the 26 DIP icon button, 4 DIP padding and gaps,
// 12 DIP from the canvas edges. test_shell_theme.cpp checks that
// tool_strip_geometry() reads exactly these.
constexpr StripGeometry kGeometry{26, 4, 4, 12};

} // namespace

TEST_CASE("the strip sits in the canvas's upper-left corner", "[jusprin][tool_strip]")
{
    const StripLayout layout = layout_tool_strip(kGeometry, 1.f, 1000.f, 700.f);

    CHECK(layout.strip.x == 12.f);
    CHECK(layout.strip.y == 12.f);
    CHECK(layout.strip.w == 158.f); // 4 + 5 * 26 + 5 * 4 + 4
    CHECK(layout.strip.h == 34.f);  // 4 + 26 + 4
}
}

// Contract tests for the viewport tool strip's layout: a row in the canvas's
// upper-left corner, and where each button sits in it, independent of the
// selection and the camera.

#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>

#include "slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Canvas/ViewportToolStripLayout.hpp"

#include <cmath>

using namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin;

namespace {

// The token file's values: the 26 DIP icon button, 4 DIP padding and gaps,
// 12 DIP from the canvas edges. test_shell_theme.cpp checks that
// tool_strip_geometry() reads exactly these.
constexpr StripGeometry kGeometry{26, 4, 4, 12};

} // namespace

TEST_CASE("the strip sits in the canvas's upper-left corner", "[jusprin][tool_strip]")
{
    const StripLayout layout = layout_tool_strip(kGeometry, 1.f, 1000.f, 700.f);

    CHECK(layout.strip.x == 12.f);
    CHECK(layout.strip.y == 12.f);
    CHECK(layout.strip.w == 158.f); // 4 + 5 * 26 + 5 * 4 + 4
    CHECK(layout.strip.h == 34.f);  // 4 + 26 + 4
}
}

// Contract tests for the viewport tool strip's layout: a row in the canvas's
// upper-left corner, and where each button sits in it, independent of the
// selection and the camera.

#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>

#include "slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Canvas/ViewportToolStripLayout.hpp"

#include <cmath>

using namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin;

namespace {

// The token file's values: the 26 DIP icon button, 4 DIP padding and gaps,
// 12 DIP from the canvas edges. test_shell_theme.cpp checks that
// tool_strip_geometry() reads exactly these.
constexpr StripGeometry kGeometry{26, 4, 4, 12};

} // namespace

TEST_CASE("the strip sits in the canvas's upper-left corner", "[jusprin][tool_strip]")
{
    const StripLayout layout = layout_tool_strip(kGeometry, 1.f, 1000.f, 700.f);

    CHECK(layout.strip.x == 12.f);
    CHECK(layout.strip.y == 12.f);
    CHECK(layout.strip.w == 158.f); // 4 + 5 * 26 + 5 * 4 + 4
    CHECK(layout.strip.h == 34.f);  // 4 + 26 + 4
}
}

// Contract tests for the viewport tool strip's layout: a row in the canvas's
// upper-left corner, and where each button sits in it, independent of the
// selection and the camera.

#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>

#include "slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Canvas/ViewportToolStripLayout.hpp"

#include <cmath>

using namespace Slic3r::GUI::JusPrin;

namespace {

// The token file's values: the 26 DIP icon button, 4 DIP padding and gaps,
// 12 DIP from the canvas edges. test_shell_theme.cpp checks that
// tool_strip_geometry() reads exactly these.
constexpr StripGeometry kGeometry{26, 4, 4, 12};

} // namespace

TEST_CASE("the strip sits in the canvas's upper-left corner", "[jusprin][tool_strip]")
{
    const StripLayout layout = layout_tool_strip(kGeometry, 1.f, 1000.f, 700.f);

    CHECK(layout.strip.x == 12.f);
    CHECK(layout.strip.y == 12.f);
    CHECK(layout.strip.w == 158.f); // 4 + 5 * 26 + 5 * 4 + 4
    CHECK(layout.strip.h == 34.f);  // 4 + 26 + 4
}
}

from pathlib import Path
import re

root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
checkout = root / 'sandboxes/toolbar-stewardship'
pattern = re.compile(r'^<<<<<<< ours\n(.*?)^=======\n(.*?)^>>>>>>> theirs\n', re.M | re.S)
for name in ('GLCanvas3D.cpp', 'GLCanvas3D.hpp'):
    path = checkout / 'src/slic3r/GUI' / name
    source = path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    def resolve(match):
        upstream, fork = match.groups()
        if 'only_body = true;' in fork:
            # Preserve the complete upstream hunk (including its new CAD grid)
            # and insert only the fork's condition before the plate draw.
            prefix = fork[:fork.index('    wxGetApp().plater()->get_partplate_list().render(')]
            assert upstream.startswith('    wxGetApp().plater()->get_partplate_list().render(')
            return prefix + upstream
        assert ('end_frame()' in upstream or 'render_item_windows' in upstream or '_overlay_signature' in upstream)
        return upstream
    source, count = pattern.subn(resolve, source)
    assert count == (3 if name.endswith('.cpp') else 1), (name, count)
    path.write_text(source, encoding='utf-8')

source = (checkout / 'src/slic3r/GUI/GLCanvas3D.cpp').read_text(encoding='utf-8')
def body(signature):
    start = source.index('{', source.index(signature))
    depth = 1
    end = start + 1
    while depth:
        depth += (source[end] == '{') - (source[end] == '}')
        end += 1
    return source[start + 1:end - 1]

toolbar = body('void GLCanvas3D::_render_overlay_toolbars()')
assert toolbar.index('if (m_legacy_overlays_hidden)') < toolbar.index('return;') < toolbar.index('_render_main_toolbar();')
assert source.count('void GLCanvas3D::_render_overlay_toolbars()') == 1
render = body('void GLCanvas3D::render(')
assert render.count('_render_overlay_toolbars();') == 1
assert render.index('m_overlay_renderer();') < render.index('end_frame()') < render.index('_render_overlay_toolbars();')
plate = body('void GLCanvas3D::_render_platelist(')
assert plate.index('only_body = true;') < plate.index('get_partplate_list().render(')
assert '!m_plate_chrome_enabled' in plate
assert 'only_body = true;' not in body('void GLCanvas3D::_render_scene(').replace('//only_body = true;', '')
assert 'render_item_windows' in body('void GLCanvas3D::_render_overlays()')
assert 'render_overlay_input_window' in body('void GLCanvas3D::_render_overlays()')
assert '<<<<<<<' not in source
print('PASS: isolated upstream replay retains both visibility policies, one toolbar pass, ImGui ordering, and upstream input windows/CAD grid.')

+# Toolbar stewardship verification
+
+Working review evidence; intentionally untracked.

+
+The Prepare toolbar's appearance, actions and value panels are unchanged.
+The fork continues to own presentation policy through
+`CanvasPresentationController`; Orca owns the drawing and manipulation code.

+The GL toolbar/layer-overlay calls move from `_render_overlays()` into
+`_render_overlay_toolbars()`, matching upstream's split. Their bodies are
+preserved, not reimplemented. A neutral visibility check inside that pass
+prevents a moved caller from bypassing the policy. The pass runs before ImGui
+is rendered. The existing fork callback remains inside the ImGui frame.
+
+The fork's `only_body` condition moves from the inline scene pass into
+`_render_platelist()`. This retains the original rendering call and its
+arguments and applies the policy at the common plate-drawing boundary.
+
+The native harness gains one friend accessor so it can measure GL samples
+produced by the toolbar pass directly. It asserts zero samples while hidden
+and positive samples in stock mode and after shell removal. This tests actual
+drawing independently of the outer frame's guard, rather than reading back
+the policy flag. No production draw counters or copied rendering algorithms
+are introduced.
+
+## Rebase evidence
+
+Fork endpoint: `ee1bb889a210e97006d1d8a5684be61c4018cbf8` plus the three changed
+source/test files. The temporary snapshot hash is recorded in

+Upstream was refreshed to `b6bb1b92c9` (the GLCanvas3D code is unchanged from
+the initially reported `61dbe5572f`). Fork base: `8500fcdcca`.
+
+Simulation:
+
+```
+git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=8500fcdcca upstream/main <temporary-snapshot>
+```
+
+Output is in `build/toolbar-merge.txt`. An independent three-way replay of the
+fork's net changes was performed in `sandboxes/toolbar-stewardship`, starting
+at upstream, with the unrelated deleted Windows build script excluded.
+This is an isolated replay, not an upstream merge into the working branch.
+
+Rendering resolutions were exercised in that checkout:
+
+1. Keep upstream's frame-cache/end-frame block. It already calls the toolbar
+   pass once. This resolution no longer loses plate presentation policy.
+2. In `_render_platelist`, keep the fork condition **and** upstream's drawing
+   call, including its new `!m_plate_chrome_enabled` argument. Taking either
+   whole side is lossy; the instruction is recorded beside the condition.
+3. Keep upstream's new arrange/gizmo/layer input-window calls in
+   `_render_overlays()`. They remain protected by the existing outer guard.
+4. Keep upstream's `_overlay_signature` declaration in the header.
+5. Git retains two helper definitions around the new `_overlay_signature`
+   implementation. This causes a compile failure rather than silent toolbar
+   leakage. Retain upstream's helper body, insert the visibility guard, and
+   remove the duplicate. This instruction is recorded at the definition.
+   The replay check compares the two bodies before combining them and proves
+   that their only substantive difference is the guard.
+
+`build/check_toolbar_replay.py` checks the resolved rendering files: one helper
+definition, one invocation per frame, the guard before toolbar drawing, the
+fork callback before `end_frame()`, the plate condition before the preserved
+upstream render call, and preservation of upstream's input-window calls.
+
+The other simulation conflicts predate this change:
+
+| File | Resolution assessment |
+| --- | --- |

+| `build_release_vs.bat` | Upstream deleted it; choosing deletion loses the fork's build script. Requires a separate Windows-build decision. Excluded only from the isolated replay, not the simulation. |
+| English `.po` | Keep both message entries. Taking a whole side loses an entry. |
+| `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt` | Keep upstream CAD sources and the JusPrin source include. |
+| `GUI_App.cpp` | A whole-side resolution is lossy: retain upstream agent resolution and reapply the Bambu fake-agent substitution at its new decision boundary. |
+| `GUI_ObjectList.cpp` | Preserve upstream's localized snapshot label in the shared renamed-object command, as its existing site comment instructs; avoid adding a second object snapshot. |
+| `Plater.cpp` | Keep both include/notification additions. The constructor overlap with upstream's textured-mesh import changes needs a deliberate resolution preserving both complete functions and project-state initialization. Taking a whole side is lossy. |
+| `Plater.hpp` | Keep both upstream filament helpers and the grouped fork declarations. |
+
+Those unrelated integration conflicts remain unresolved in the scratch checkout.
+This work does not claim a completed or fully built upstream update.
+

+
+The first baseline build failed because MSBuild inherited both `Path` and
+`PATH`. Recreating the process variable with the spelling `Path` resolved that
+environment problem; no repository build settings were changed.
+
+Only Windows is exercised here. macOS/Linux and the upstream frame-caching

# AGENTS.md instructions for C:\src\JusPrin

<INSTRUCTIONS>
These AGENTS.md instructions replace all previously provided AGENTS.md instructions.

# CLAUDE.md

OrcaSlicer — open-source C++17 3D slicer. wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

</INSTRUCTIONS>

- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

# Toolbar stewardship verification

Working review evidence; intentionally untracked.

## Change and ownership

The Prepare toolbar's appearance, actions and value panels are unchanged.
The fork continues to own presentation policy through
`CanvasPresentationController`; Orca owns the drawing and manipulation code.

The GL toolbar/layer-overlay calls move from `_render_overlays()` into
`_render_overlay_toolbars()`, matching upstream's split. Their bodies are
preserved, not reimplemented. A neutral visibility check inside that pass
prevents a moved caller from bypassing the policy. The pass runs before ImGui
is rendered. The existing fork callback remains inside the ImGui frame.

The fork's `only_body` condition moves from the inline scene pass into
`_render_platelist()`. This retains the original rendering call and its
arguments and applies the policy at the common plate-drawing boundary.

The native harness gains one friend accessor so it can measure GL samples
produced by the toolbar pass directly. It asserts zero samples while hidden
and positive samples in stock mode and after shell removal. This tests actual
drawing independently of the outer frame's guard, rather than reading back
the policy flag. No production draw counters or copied rendering algorithms
are introduced.

## Rebase evidence

Fork endpoint: `ee1bb889a210e97006d1d8a5684be61c4018cbf8` plus the four changed
source/test files. The final temporary snapshot is
`126b8f323ca8f50f74f5169cb5ca2921f78577ef`, also recorded in
`build/toolbar-simulation-commit.txt`; the normal index and branch are unchanged.
Upstream was refreshed to `b6bb1b92c9` (the GLCanvas3D code is unchanged from
the initially reported `61dbe5572f`). Fork base: `8500fcdcca`.

Simulation:

```
git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=8500fcdcca upstream/main <temporary-snapshot>
```

Output is in `build/toolbar-merge.txt`. An independent three-way replay of the
fork's net changes was performed in `sandboxes/toolbar-stewardship`, starting
at upstream, with the unrelated deleted Windows build script excluded.
This is an isolated replay, not an upstream merge into the working branch.

Rendering resolutions were exercised in that checkout:

1. Keep upstream's frame-cache/end-frame block. It already calls the toolbar
   pass once. This resolution no longer loses plate presentation policy.
2. In `_render_platelist`, keep the fork condition **and** upstream's drawing
   call, including its new `!m_plate_chrome_enabled` argument. Taking either
   whole side is lossy; the instruction is recorded beside the condition.
3. Keep upstream's new arrange/gizmo/layer input-window calls in
   `_render_overlays()`. They remain protected by the existing outer guard.
4. Keep upstream's `_overlay_signature` declaration in the header.
5. Git retains two helper definitions around the new `_overlay_signature`
   implementation. This causes a compile failure rather than silent toolbar
   leakage. Retain upstream's helper body, insert the visibility guard, and
   remove the duplicate. This instruction is recorded at the definition.
   The replay check compares the two bodies before combining them and proves
   that their only substantive difference is the guard.

`build/check_toolbar_replay.py` checks the resolved rendering files: one helper
definition, one invocation per frame, the guard before toolbar drawing, the
fork callback before `end_frame()`, the plate condition before the preserved
upstream render call, and preservation of upstream's input-window calls.

The other simulation conflicts predate this change:

| File | Resolution assessment |
| --- | --- |
| `AGENTS.md` | Keep both documentation/testing instructions, reconciling their distinct temporary-document policies by scope. |
| `build_release_vs.bat` | Upstream deleted it; choosing deletion loses the fork's build script. Requires a separate Windows-build decision. Excluded only from the isolated replay, not the simulation. |
| English `.po` | Keep both message entries. Taking a whole side loses an entry. |
| `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt` | Keep upstream CAD sources and the JusPrin source include. |
| `GUI_App.cpp` | A whole-side resolution is lossy: retain upstream agent resolution and reapply the Bambu fake-agent substitution at its new decision boundary. |
| `GUI_ObjectList.cpp` | Preserve upstream's localized snapshot label in the shared renamed-object command, as its existing site comment instructs; avoid adding a second object snapshot. |
| `Plater.cpp` | Keep both include/notification additions. The constructor overlap with upstream's textured-mesh import changes needs a deliberate resolution preserving both complete functions and project-state initialization. Taking a whole side is lossy. |
| `Plater.hpp` | Keep both upstream filament helpers and the grouped fork declarations. |

Those unrelated integration conflicts were not resolved. The scratch checkout
was removed after verification; the resolved rendering files are retained in
`build/toolbar-replay-resolved/` and can be regenerated by the check script.
This work does not claim a completed or fully built upstream update.

## Verification

- GUI-free JusPrin contracts: 50 cases, 266 assertions passed.
- Agent page: 15 files, 201 tests passed.
- Brand guards: passed, with the existing expected-failure contrast case
  (`focus ring and tertiary text stay visible on the selected surface`).
- Isolated resolved-rendering replay check: passed.
- Full Windows Release `ALL_BUILD`: passed (`build/toolbar-build-complete.log`).
- Agent native contracts: 259 cases, 4,817 assertions passed. The first broad

## Change and ownership

The Prepare toolbar's appearance, actions and value panels are unchanged.
The fork continues to own presentation policy through
`CanvasPresentationController`; Orca owns the drawing and manipulation code.

The GL toolbar/layer-overlay calls move from `_render_overlays()` into
`_render_overlay_toolbars()`, matching upstream's split. Their bodies are
preserved, not reimplemented. A neutral visibility check inside that pass
prevents a moved caller from bypassing the policy. The pass runs before ImGui
is rendered. The existing fork callback remains inside the ImGui frame.

The fork's `only_body` condition moves from the inline scene pass into
`_render_platelist()`. This retains the original rendering call and its
arguments and applies the policy at the common plate-drawing boundary.
